preconditions.description: Attacker must hold some amount of the dividend token (CAKE or DOGE) to transfer to the dividend tracker contract
The dividend tracker contracts (CakeDividendTracker and DogeDividendTracker) must have been deployed and be operational

violation_target.exploit_hint: Call the vulnerable distributeDividends(uint256 amount) function on either CakeDividendTracker or DogeDividendTracker contract with a fake amount. First, transfer some dividend tokens (CAKE/DOGE) to the tracker contract, then call distributeDividends with that amount. This will artificially inflate magnifiedDividendPerShare, allowing you to withdraw more dividends than you're entitled to. The attack path: 1. Transfer small amount of dividend token to tracker contract, 2. Call distributeDividends with that amount, 3. Withdraw dividends using claim() to receive inflated payout.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The distributeDividends(uint256 amount) function in DividendPayingToken is public and lacks access control. It doesn't verify that the caller actually transferred the dividend tokens to the contract. An attacker can transfer a small amount of dividend token, then call distributeDividends with a much larger amount, artificially inflating magnifiedDividendPerShare and allowing them to withdraw more dividends than entitled.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Acquire CAKE tokens and DCAKE tokens. 2. Transfer small amount of CAKE to CakeDividendTracker. 3. Call distributeDividends with large amount to inflate magnifiedDividendPerShare. 4. Claim inflated dividends via claim() function.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use deal() to give attacker CAKE tokens. 2. Get DCAKE tokens by buying from Uniswap or minting (if possible). 3. Transfer small CAKE amount to CakeDividendTracker. 4. Call distributeDividends with large amount. 5. Call claim() to withdraw inflated dividends.
